environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with AWS Verified Access instance attached. The Verified Access trust provider is configured with IAM Identity Center (SSO) using Cedar policy language. The Cedar policy evaluates context.http.request.url.path against a resource-ownership mapping maintained in a DynamoDB policy store. Specifically, the Cedar policy denies any request where the principal's identity-store user-id does not match the resource owner attribute resolved via a policy-information-point (PIP) lookup keyed on the URL path parameter (document ID). The Verified Access endpoint policy is: `permit(principal, action, resource) when { resource.owner == principal.identitystore.userId };` with a PIP resolver that maps /api/documents/{id} to the DynamoDB item {PK: 'DOC#{id}', owner: '<user-id>'}. Additionally, the ALB is configured to ONLY accept traffic from the Verified Access ENI (security group ingress restricted to the VA endpoint's security group), making direct ALB access impossible without passing through Verified Access policy evaluation.

config.cedar_policy: permit(principal, action, resource) when { resource.owner == principal.identitystore.userId };
config.pip_resolver: DynamoDB table 'doc-ownership' with PK='DOC#<doc_id>' containing 'owner' attribute mapped to identity-store userId
config.verified_access_log_config: OCSF format to CloudWatch Logs with real-time evaluation
config.direct_alb_access: blocked by security group - only VA endpoint ENI allowed
